organic_farming.name: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)
organic_farming.summary: Government scheme to promote organic farming through cluster-based approach. Provides financial assistance of ₹50,000 per hectare over 3 years for organic inputs, certification, labeling, packaging, and marketing support.
eligibility: Farmer groups with minimum 20 hectares cluster
Valid land records and Aadhaar
Willingness to adopt organic practices for 3+ years
applicationProcess: Contact your District Agriculture Officer
Form a cluster of farmers (50 or more in 20+ hectares)
Apply through State Agriculture Department
Undergo PGS (Participatory Guarantee System) certification

organic_farming.name: PM-KISAN Samman Nidhi
organic_farming.summary: Income support scheme providing ₹6,000 per year to all landholding farmer families. Amount is paid in three equal installments of ₹2,000 every four months directly to the farmer's bank account.
eligibility: All landholding farmer families
Valid Aadhaar linked to bank account
Not a government employee or income tax payer
applicationProcess: Visit pmkisan.gov.in or nearest CSC center
Click 'New Farmer Registration'
Enter Aadhaar, bank details, and land info
Verification done by State Nodal Officer

organic_farming.name: Mission Organic Value Chain Development (MOVCDNER)
organic_farming.summary: Scheme for NE region focused on development of certified organic production in a value chain mode. Provides support for organic inputs, quality seeds, and post-harvest management including FPO development.
organic_farming.benefits: Up to ₹2 Crore per FPO for value chain development
eligibility: Farmers in North Eastern states
Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs)
Minimum 200 hectares cluster formation
applicationProcess: Register with State Agriculture Department
Form or join a Farmer Producer Organization
Submit project proposal through State Mission Director

organic_farming.name: National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA)
organic_farming.summary: Promotes sustainable agriculture through climate-resilient practices. Offers financial support for soil health management, rainfed area development, and on-farm water management to improve farm productivity.
eligibility: All farmers with cultivable land
Priority to SC/ST and small/marginal farmers
Land should be under rainfed/dry farming
applicationProcess: Apply through District Agriculture Office
Submit land records and farmer ID
Selection as per state government criteria

organic_farming.name: Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM)
organic_farming.summary: Provides subsidies for purchase of agricultural machinery and equipment. Farmers can get 40-50% subsidy on tractors, tillers, sprayers, harvesters and other farm equipment from empanelled manufacturers.
organic_farming.benefits: 40-50% subsidy on farm machinery (up to ₹5 Lakh)
eligibility: Individual farmers with valid land holding
SC/ST/Small/Marginal farmers get higher subsidy
One machine per farmer per category
applicationProcess: Register on AGRIMACHINERY portal (agrimachinery.nic.in)
Select machinery from empanelled list
Upload documents: Aadhaar, land records, bank passbook
Subsidy disbursed via DBT after purchase verification

rainwater_farming.name: Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana (PMKSY)
rainwater_farming.ministry: Ministry of Agriculture & Ministry of Jal Shakti
rainwater_farming.summary: Flagship scheme for 'Har Khet Ko Paani' – ensures access to protective irrigation for all farms. Provides 55-100% subsidy on micro-irrigation systems including drip and sprinkler, rainwater harvesting structures, and farm ponds.
rainwater_farming.benefits: 55-100% subsidy on micro-irrigation (₹1-5 Lakh per unit)
eligibility: All farmers with cultivable land
Small and marginal farmers get higher subsidy (100%)
Land should have water source or potential for harvesting
applicationProcess: Apply through State Agriculture/Horticulture Department
Register on PMKSY portal or visit Krishi Vigyan Kendra
Submit land records, water source details
Technical survey and approval by district committee

rainwater_farming.name: MGNREGA – Farm Pond / Water Harvesting
rainwater_farming.summary: Under MGNREGA, farmers can get free farm ponds, check dams, and rainwater harvesting structures built on their land. Labour costs are fully covered, and material costs are subsidized. Excellent for rainfed areas.
rainwater_farming.benefits: 100% labour cost + material allowance (up to ₹3 Lakh per structure)
eligibility: Job card holder under MGNREGA
Land in rainfed / drought-prone areas
SC/ST and small farmers get priority
applicationProcess: Apply at Gram Panchayat with MGNREGA job card
Request farm pond / water harvesting under Individual Beneficiary scheme
Technical approval by Block Development Officer

rainwater_farming.name: NMSA – Rainfed Area Development (RAD)
rainwater_farming.summary: Specifically targets rainfed areas with integrated farming system approach. Provides support for soil moisture conservation, rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharging, and drought-proofing activities.
rainwater_farming.benefits: Up to ₹1.5 Lakh per hectare for integrated activities
eligibility: Farmers in identified rainfed areas
Cluster-based approach with community participation
Priority to tribal and drought-prone districts

Identified through watershed development programs
Community mobilization and cluster formation

integrated_farming.ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
integrated_farming.summary: Dedicated scheme for fisheries development. Provides 40-60% subsidy for fresh water fish farming, pond construction, hatchery setup, biofloc units, and cage culture. Aims to double fisheries production and exports.
integrated_farming.benefits: 40-60% subsidy (up to ₹25 Lakh for pond construction, ₹50 Lakh for RAS units)

integrated_farming.name: Blue Revolution (Neel Kranti Mission)
integrated_farming.summary: Comprehensive scheme for integrated development of inland and marine fisheries. Covers pond construction, feed mills, cold chain infrastructure, ornamental fisheries, and seaweed cultivation.
integrated_farming.benefits: 50-80% subsidy based on component and category

integrated_farming.name: RKVY – Integrated Farming System

featured.title: Organic Farming Success: Earning ₹50 Lakh Per Year from 5 Acres
featured.summary: This inspiring documentary follows Rajesh Sharma from Punjab who transitioned his 5-acre conventional farm to 100% organic over 3 years. He now earns ₹50 lakh annually by growing organic wheat, basmati rice, and vegetables. Key to his success: vermicompost preparation, neem-based pest control, crop rotation with legumes, and direct marketing through organic cooperatives. His input costs dropped by 60% while selling prices increased 40% through organic certification (PGS India).
keyTakeaways: Started with just 1 acre pilot, proved profitability before scaling
60% lower input costs using farm-made compost and bio-pesticides
PGS certification took 3 years but increased selling prices by 40%
Direct-to-consumer via cooperatives eliminates middlemen
Crop rotation with mustard and lentils maintains soil nitrogen naturally

featured.title: Rainwater Harvesting Revolution: How One Village Beat Drought Forever
featured.summary: A powerful documentary showing how Hiware Bazar village in Maharashtra transformed from a drought-hit, migration-prone village to a model of water sustainability. Through community-led rainwater harvesting — check dams, contour trenches, farm ponds, and rooftop collection — they raised groundwater levels by 15 feet in just 5 years. Per-capita income went from ₹830 to ₹30,000, and 60 families that had migrated returned. Government MGNREGA funds were used for construction.
keyTakeaways: Community approach: entire village participated in watershed management
Used MGNREGA funds — zero personal cost for construction
Groundwater rose by 15 feet within 5 years of rainwater harvesting
Per-capita income increased 36x — from ₹830 to ₹30,000
Farm ponds + contour bunding + check dams = complete water security

featured.title: Integrated Fish Farming: ₹20 Lakh Profit from 2 Acre Pond
featured.summary: Meet Suresh Yadav from Bihar who combines fish farming with poultry, duckery, and vegetable cultivation on just 2 acres. His integrated model produces 8 tonnes of fish, 2,000 eggs monthly, and 500kg vegetables per season. The genius is in the synergy — poultry waste feeds the fish, fish pond water irrigates vegetables, and duck droppings enrich the pond. Total investment was ₹8 Lakh (₹5 Lakh covered by PMMSY subsidy), now earning ₹22 Lakh/year net profit.
keyTakeaways: Integrated model: fish + poultry + duckery + vegetables on 2 acres
₹5 Lakh PMMSY subsidy covered 60% of initial investment
Zero waste cycle: poultry feeds fish, fish water irrigates crops
8 tonnes of fish per year from Rohu, Catla, and Mrigal polyculture
ROI achieved in 14 months — now ₹22 Lakh/year net profit
